exact_cell_changes.after: Passed House 2025-01-23 (57-Y 40-N); passed Senate with substitute 2025-02-12; conference report agreed to by Senate 2025-02-21 and House 2025-02-22; enrolled 2025-03-07; House rejected Governor's recommended amendments 2025-04-02 (11-Y 85-N); vetoed by Governor 2025-05-02. The April2 return followed rejection of recommended amendments during the2025 reconvened session. ArticleVsection6(c)(iii) makes the Governor’s May2veto of a returned bill final: that veto stands and the bill does not become law; this is distinct from the ordinary override procedure.

exact_cell_changes.before: Enrolled HB1601 would require a locality, before approval of specified zoning applications for a new high energy use facility, to require the applicant to assess its sound profile on residential units and schools within 500 feet of the property boundary, to the extent practicable and within the statutory timeline. A facility qualifies when the applicant reasonably anticipates at application that it will require 100 MW or more of retail utility power. The locality may require specified resource assessments on the site or immediately contiguous land, and must require qualified utility substation and transmission information. The existing-approval expansion or modification exception states that the expansion 'does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more'; its numeric boundary is unresolved. Existing local zoning authority is preserved. The enrolled print has blank chapter and approval fields; later post-veto proceedings remain unverified.

The locality may require specified resource assessments on the site or immediately contiguous land, and must require qualified utility substation and transmission information. The existing-approval expansion or modification exception states that the expansion 'does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more'; its numeric boundary is unresolved. Existing local zoning authority is preserved. The enrolled print has blank chapter and approval fields; the retained returned-bill sequence and ArticleVsection6(c)(iii) establish the final May2veto rather than an operative statute. The expansion-boundary wording remains an explicit ambiguity in the failed enrolled proposal, not a current legal requirement.
